summary: Game crashes when replacing a block with a wall with blockstate up:false
description: Give yourself a wall using give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1 Then, place a block with no other blocks around it, and press left and right click at the same time while looking at that block and holding the wall. Then, crash.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Ensure you are in Creative mode by executing the command `/gamemode creative`.
3. Give yourself a brick wall with the specific blockstate using the command `give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1`.
4. Place any block on the ground such that there are no other blocks around it.
5. Hold the brick wall in your hand and aim at the placed block.
6. Press left click and right click simultaneously while looking at the placed block.
7. Observe that the game crashes under these conditions.
Observed Behavior:
When attempting to replace a block with a brick wall having the `up:false` blockstate, the game crashes under specific conditions. To reproduce the issue, first give yourself a brick wall item using the command `/give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1`. Next, place this brick wall in an open area where no other blocks are nearby. While holding the brick wall and looking at the placed block, press both left and right mouse buttons simultaneously. This action triggers a crash, halting gameplay immediately.

This detailed sequence of steps should help developers understand and replicate the issue accurately.
Expected Behavior: When following the steps, the game should not crash. Instead, placing the brick wall with blockstate `up:false` next to a solitary block while holding left and right click simultaneously should simply result in the wall being placed without any adverse effects. The game should remain stable and functional throughout this action.
